steps.title: Register the app in Entra
steps.detail: Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center as at least an Application Developer, go to Entra ID, App registrations, New registration, enter a name, choose supported account types, and register. Record the Application (client) ID and Directory (tenant) ID from Overview.
steps.blockerTip: New registrations are hidden to users by default. Do not assume the app is visible until you check Enterprise apps.

steps.title: Add API permissions, minimum only
steps.detail: Add permissions, choose Microsoft Graph, then Delegated permissions for a user sign-in app. Add only what the feature uses, for example User.Read, plus offline_access if you need a refresh token.
steps.blockerTip: Application permissions are for app-only flows, not user sign-in. Picking the wrong type is a common first failure.

steps.title: Create a client secret, server side only
steps.detail: Under Certificates and secrets, create a client secret, copy it at once, and store it in a secrets manager. It is shown only at creation in most flows.
steps.blockerTip: Never put the secret in client code or a public repo. If you lose it, create a new one and delete the old one.

steps.title: Add the exact redirect URI
steps.detail: Under Authentication, add a Web platform redirect URI that matches your code exactly, including host, path, and https. Use localhost only for local testing.
steps.blockerTip: A redirect mismatch stops sign-in. The URI in code and in Entra must match character for character.

steps.title: Get admin consent, then test sign-in
steps.detail: Ask an admin to Grant admin consent for the tenant if the permissions need it, then test sign-in with a real account and one API call, for example a profile read.
steps.blockerTip: If consent is missing, users see a consent error, not a code error. Check API permissions and consent status first.
